candidates.name: Haluski and Kielbasa (Cabbage and Egg Noodles)
candidates.why: Named as a P2 hunting-ground target and nothing haluski-like is in the catalog. Buttery cabbage + egg noodles + smoked sausage is a one-skillet dish that weighs and divides cleanly at 14. Every ingredient is a tracked commodity (kielbasa, cabbage, egg-noodles, onions, butter). CONFIDENCE: source is 387 cal / 13g protein at 10 servings, which is under target; our version needs roughly a 2:1 bump of kielbasa to noodles plus cottage cheese or a leaner butter hand to land 500+ cal at 28g protein. Source numbers verified from the page, our numbers are projected.

candidates.name: Kielbasa Cabbage and Potato Skillet
candidates.why: Source verifies 508 cal / 20g protein per serving already, so it clears the calorie bar as written and only needs a modest sausage bump for 25g+. Five ingredients, all board commodities, no substitutions needed. Pure weigh-and-divide skillet, ideal at 14 servings. Distinct from the sheet-pan brats entry (stovetop, cabbage-forward, no peppers).

candidates.name: Bigos (Polish Hunter's Stew)
candidates.why: The flagship Polish sausage-and-cabbage stew and the catalog has zero Polish entries. Long simmer, gets better reheated, which is exactly the meal-prep profile. Signature ingredients (sauerkraut, cabbage, kielbasa, pork-shoulder) are all board-tracked; the four flags are aromatics and garnish-tier items that can be dropped or swapped (fresh mushrooms for porcini, dried-thyme/bay for juniper and marjoram) without changing the dish. CONFIDENCE: source is 335 cal / 14g at 8 servings and uses chicken thighs as the meat; our version goes pork-shoulder-and-kielbasa only and portions heavier, so est_cal is projected, not verified.

candidates.name: Szegedin Goulash (Pork and Sauerkraut Paprika Stew)
candidates.why: Verified on the source page at 649 cal / 35g protein per serving, so it clears both bars without adjustment. Genuinely distinct from the live American Goulash Pasta (that is ground beef and macaroni; this is a paprika-and-sauerkraut braise) and from Hungarian Chicken Paprikash (different protein, sauerkraut base, no noodles). Braise-and-divide over egg noodles or potatoes scales fine at 14. Only caraway is off-board and it is optional.

candidates.name: Hungarian Pork and Potato Goulash (Porkolt)
candidates.why: Verified 560 cal / 41g protein at the source, one of the highest protein-to-calorie ratios in this slice. Potatoes are in the pot so there is no separate starch to portion. All seven main ingredients are board commodities. Distinct dish from Szegedin (no sauerkraut, no sour cream) and from the live American Goulash Pasta.

candidates.name: Fasolka po Bretonsku (Polish Baked Beans with Kielbasa)
candidates.why: Slow-simmered bean-and-sausage stew, cheapest protein-per-dollar build in the slice, and the catalog has no pork-and-bean dinner at all. Source verifies 515 cal at 6 servings so calories are fine. Butter beans are not a board id but canned-white-beans is the direct substitute and carries the same math. CONFIDENCE: source protein is only 13g per serving, so our version must roughly double the kielbasa (and lean on the beans) to reach 25g+; protein figure is projected, not verified.

candidates.name: Polish Leczo (Kielbasa and Peppers Stew)
candidates.why: Verified 571 cal / 29g protein at the source, clears both bars as written. Every ingredient is board-tracked and bell peppers plus onions are the cheapest produce on the board most weeks. Distinct from the live Italian Sausage Penne with Peppers: no pasta, smoked kielbasa instead of Italian sausage, paprika-tomato base served over rice. Simmer-and-ladle, trivially scalable.

candidates.name: Kapusniak (Polish Cabbage and Sausage Soup)
candidates.why: Rounds out the Polish block with a soup format the catalog does not have on the pork side. Cheap, freezes well, reheats better than it cooks. Parsnip is the only off-board item and carrots cover it. CONFIDENCE: the source page lists no nutrition at all and a broth-based cabbage soup is naturally light, so this only qualifies if our build adds potatoes and roughly a pound of kielbasa per 14 servings; est_cal is entirely projected. Lowest-confidence entry in this slice and a fair one to cut if the pool is over target.

candidates.name: Senfbraten (German Mustard-Gravy Pork Roast)
candidates.why: Verified 417 cal / 53g protein at the source, an outstanding protein ratio; adding the potato or noodle side our format requires puts it comfortably over 500 cal. The catalog has no German entry at all. Slow braise, slices and weighs out cleanly at 14. Source calls for a pork loin roast which has no dedicated board id, so pork-shoulder (tracked) is the budget swap; the white wine is optional and beef-broth carries the gravy.

candidates.name: Bratwurst and Sauerkraut with Potatoes
candidates.why: Uses the bratwurst commodity, which nothing in the live catalog touches, and pairs it with sauerkraut and red-potatoes (both tracked). Dump-and-bake construction is about as batch-friendly as it gets. CONFIDENCE: source is 436 cal / 17g protein at 5 servings, under both bars, so our version bumps to two brats per serving and adds a mustard-cream finish; est_cal projected. Beer is the only off-board item and chicken-broth substitutes directly.

candidates.name: Pierogi and Kielbasa Casserole
candidates.why: Verified 769 cal / 36g protein at the source, clears both bars with room to spare. Dump-and-bake casserole, cuts and weighs out perfectly at 14. FLAGGED: frozen pierogies are the signature ingredient and have no board home, which is a real cost-tracking gap; the fallback is to build it on potato-gnocchi (tracked) or egg-noodles-plus-potato, but that changes the dish. Worth keeping only if the mapper can register a pierogi commodity.

candidates.name: Creamy Kielbasa and Potato Soup
candidates.why: Source verifies 494 cal per serving, essentially at the bar already. All eight ingredients are board commodities and the base (potatoes, carrots, celery, corn) is cheap year-round. Distinct from Zuppa Toscana (smoked kielbasa and paprika rather than Italian sausage, bacon and kale). CONFIDENCE: source protein is 14g, so our version needs roughly 1.5x the kielbasa plus a cottage-cheese or evaporated-milk thickener to reach 25g+; protein projected.

candidates.name: Sheet-Pan Bratwurst with Peppers and Potatoes
candidates.why: Verified 512 cal / 22g protein at the source, so calories clear and protein needs only a small bump. Second bratwurst dish and the only sheet-pan entry with peppers, which keeps it distinct from the cabbage-and-potato skillet. All ingredients board-tracked. Sheet-pan roasting is the single easiest format to double for 14 servings.

candidates.name: Sausage, Cabbage and Apple Skillet
candidates.why: Sweet-tart apple-and-mustard angle that nothing in the catalog covers, and apples are a board commodity that almost no dinner recipe currently uses. Verified 469 cal / 16g at the source. CONFIDENCE: needs a sausage increase and a served-over-potatoes or egg-noodles base to hit 500+ cal at 25g protein; est_cal projected. Skillet format, scales clean.

candidates.name: Sheet-Pan Sausage Meatballs with Kale and Potatoes
candidates.why: Verified 919 cal / 23g protein at the source (Budget Bytes also publishes a $3.46-per-serving cost, which fits the brand). Our version trims the oil to land near 700 cal while pushing protein past 25g. All ingredients board-tracked. Rolling meatballs is batch work but they cook on a sheet pan and portion by count-plus-weight, unlike stuffed or fried-to-order dishes. Distinct from the live turkey and beef meatball entries by protein and by the sheet-pan-with-greens format.

candidates.name: One-Pan Sausage Bake with Potatoes and Onion Gravy
candidates.why: Verified 649 cal / 26g protein at the source, clears both bars as written. Gravy is built in the same pan so there is no second pot. All eight ingredients board-tracked. Distinct from Bangers and Mash (roasted vegetables and pan gravy rather than mashed potatoes and onion gravy) though the selector should confirm it wants both.

candidates.name: Baked Sausage and Egg Breakfast Hash
candidates.why: Verified 723 cal / 29g protein at the source, clears both bars comfortably. Puts the breakfast-sausage and eggs commodities to work, neither of which appears in a live dinner recipe. Oven bake, weighs and divides. Breakfast-for-dinner is a genuinely open lane in the catalog.

candidates.name: Sausage Hash Brown and Egg Casserole
candidates.why: Verified 560 cal / 31g protein at the source, clears both bars with no adjustment, and it is only five ingredients, all board commodities. Make-ahead casserole is the single most meal-prep-native format on this list. Distinct from the sausage breakfast hash (bound custard casserole with hash browns and cheddar vs. roasted potato hash with cracked eggs), though the selector may want only one of the two breakfast bakes.

candidates.name: Cheesy Smoked Sausage and Rice Skillet
candidates.why: Verified 589 cal / 22g protein at the source, calories clear and protein needs a small sausage bump. All eight ingredients board-tracked and rice plus broccoli keeps the per-serving cost low. Deliberately picked over the jambalaya-style sausage rice recipes because the live Cajun Chicken and Sausage Jambalaya makes those near-duplicates; this one is a cheesy broccoli-rice skillet with no Cajun profile.

candidates.name: Red Beans and Rice with Smoked Sausage
candidates.why: Louisiana staple the catalog does not have, and it is one of the cheapest 25g-protein dinners that exists. Verified 373 cal / 22g at 8 servings, so our version portions larger to clear 500 cal. Andouille has no board id; kielbasa (tracked) plus cajun-seasoning (tracked) is the standard budget substitution and the source itself names smoked sausage or kielbasa as valid. Distinct from the live jambalaya: bean-based, no tomato-rice cook, no chicken. CONFIDENCE: est_cal projected from a larger portion, not the source figure.

candidates.name: Italian Sausage and Rice Casserole
candidates.why: Dump-and-bake rice casserole, all seven ingredients board-tracked, and the rice cooks in the dish so there is no second pot. Verified 418 cal / 19g at the source. CONFIDENCE: needs roughly 1.5x the sausage and a cheese layer to clear 500 cal at 25g+; est_cal projected. Distinct from the live Italian Sausage Penne with Peppers by base (rice, not pasta) and by construction (oven casserole, not skillet).

candidates.name: Tuscan White Bean and Sausage Soup
candidates.why: Verified 467 cal / 27g protein at the source, protein already clears and calories land at 500+ with our portion size. All eight ingredients board-tracked, canned-white-beans keeps cost per serving very low. Freezes for two months per the source, which suits the meal-prep audience. Distinct from Zuppa Toscana (tomato-and-bean broth, no cream, no potatoes).

candidates.name: Zuppa Toscana (Sausage, Potato and Kale Soup)
candidates.why: Verified 669 cal / 20g protein at the source, calories clear easily and protein needs a modest sausage bump. Recognizable copycat dish (Olive Garden) that pulls search traffic, all ingredients board-tracked, and the catalog has no creamy pork soup. Simmer-and-ladle, scales linearly to 14.

candidates.name: Spicy Vodka Rigatoni with Italian Sausage
candidates.why: Creamy tomato pasta with a heat angle the catalog does not have on the pork side. Both flags are optional: red-pepper-flakes (tracked) replaces the Calabrian chilis and the vodka can be omitted entirely without changing the sauce meaningfully. Distinct from the live Italian Sausage Penne with Peppers (cream-and-tomato-paste sauce, no bell peppers, rigatoni). CONFIDENCE: the source page publishes no nutrition data at all, so est_cal and the protein claim are both projected from the ingredient list, not verified.

candidates.name: Orecchiette with Italian Sausage and Broccoli
candidates.why: Verified 599 cal / 26g protein at the source, clears both bars as written with no adjustment. Eight ingredients, all board-tracked, and broccoli is one of the cheapest vegetables on the board. Classic Puglian pairing the catalog does not have. Toss-and-divide pasta, scales cleanly.

candidates.name: Spicy Italian Sausage Orzo
candidates.why: Verified 548 cal / 19g protein at the source; calories clear, protein needs a sausage bump. One-pot (orzo cooks in the sauce), which is the cheapest possible cleanup and scales without a colander step. Orzo is flagged only as a pasta shape the board does not price separately; the generic pasta commodity carries the cost. Distinct from the rigatoni and penne entries by grain-shape base and by being a true one-pot.

candidates.name: Creamy Italian Sausage and Mushroom Pasta
candidates.why: Verified 875 cal / 27g protein at the source; protein clears and our version trims the cream to land near 640 cal. Mushrooms are board-tracked and this is the only mushroom-forward pork pasta in the pool. White wine is the one off-board item and chicken-broth plus a splash of lemon-juice (both tracked) substitutes directly. Distinct from the live Creamy Mushroom Pork Chops over Mashed Potatoes by cut, format and base.

candidates.name: Kielbasa Mac and Cheese Bake
candidates.why: Verified 788 cal / 33g protein at the source, clears both bars easily and our version trims the cheese slightly toward 700. All eight ingredients board-tracked and mac-and-cheese is one of the cheapest bases on the board. The catalog has no mac-and-cheese bake at any protein. Baked casserole, cuts and weighs out at 14.

candidates.name: One-Pot Creamy Cajun Sausage Pasta
candidates.why: Verified 736 cal / 32g protein at the source, clears both bars as written. True one-pot: the pasta cooks in the sauce. Andouille has no board id but kielbasa plus cajun-seasoning (both tracked) is the standard swap. Distinct from the live Creamy Cajun Chicken Penne Skillet Bowls by protein and from Italian Sausage Penne by seasoning profile and smoked sausage; the selector should confirm it is comfortable with two creamy-Cajun pastas in the catalog.

candidates.name: Italian Sausage and Spinach Pasta
candidates.why: The lightest-sauce pasta in the pool (broth and parmesan, no cream), which gives the slice range instead of five cream sauces. Verified 489 cal / 20g at the source. CONFIDENCE: needs a sausage bump to clear 500 cal at 25g+; est_cal projected. White wine is optional and extra chicken-broth covers it. Spinach is board-tracked.

candidates.name: Dump-and-Bake Smoked Sausage Noodle Casserole
candidates.why: Verified 528 cal / 19g protein at 8 servings; calories clear, protein needs a sausage bump. Zero pre-cooking (no boiling the pasta, no browning the sausage) makes it the lowest-effort entry in the slice, which is a real selling point for the audience. Both condensed soups, peas and cheese are board commodities. French fried onions are a garnish-tier flag and can be dropped.

candidates.name: Italian Sausage Minestrone
candidates.why: Verified 428 cal / 22.9g protein at the source; our portion size takes it over 500 cal and a sausage bump clears 25g. Every ingredient including artichoke-hearts and chickpeas is board-tracked, which is unusual for a vegetable-heavy soup. Distinct from the two other Italian soups in the pool: no cream, no potatoes, pasta-and-bean base.

candidates.name: Italian Sausage and Lentils
candidates.why: Verified 326 cal / 22.9g protein at the source, an excellent protein ratio and the cheapest protein-per-dollar build in the slice; our version portions up and adds sausage to clear 500 cal at 25g+. FLAGGED: lentils are the base ingredient and have no board id, which is a genuine gap the mapper should consider registering (dried lentils are one of the cheapest proteins in any store). Fennel bulb is optional and celery plus the fennel already in Italian sausage covers it. CONFIDENCE: est_cal projected, not the source figure.

candidates.name: Bangers and Mash with Onion Gravy
candidates.why: Verified 666 cal / 36.4g protein at the source, clears both bars with no adjustment. All eight ingredients board-tracked and potatoes plus onions are the two cheapest staples on the board. Third bratwurst dish and the only British entry in the whole catalog. Mash-and-gravy portions by weight without any per-plate assembly.

candidates.name: Curried Sausages with Rice
candidates.why: Verified 569 cal / 28g protein at the source, clears both bars as written. Curry-powder, frozen-peas and carrots are all board-tracked and this is a genuinely cheap build. Distinct from every curry in the catalog (all chicken, beef or turkey; none use whole sausages in a curry gravy). Braise-and-ladle over rice, scales linearly.

candidates.name: Ham and White Bean Soup
candidates.why: Verified 397 cal / 31g protein at the source, an excellent protein ratio; our portion size clears 500 cal. Puts the deli-ham commodity to work, which no live dinner recipe uses. Both flags are format issues rather than missing foods: a meaty ham bone is not board-tracked (diced deli-ham or a tracked ham steak substitutes) and dried beans are not tracked separately (canned-white-beans is). CONFIDENCE: est_cal projected from a larger portion.

candidates.name: Ham Fried Rice
candidates.why: Verified 526 cal / 30g protein at the source, clears both bars with no adjustment. Every ingredient board-tracked and it is among the cheapest per-serving dinners in the pool. Distinct from the live Ground Beef Fried Rice Bowls by protein. Wok-and-divide, scales in two batches. Second use of the deli-ham commodity, which is currently dead weight on the board.

candidates.name: Italian Sausage and Sweet Potato Soup
candidates.why: Uses sweet-potatoes, a board commodity barely touched by the live catalog, in a broth soup rather than the usual bowl format. All seven ingredients tracked. Verified 376 cal / 14g at the source. CONFIDENCE: this is the biggest gap-to-target of the soups; our build needs roughly double the sausage and a bean or cream addition to clear 500 cal at 25g protein, so both numbers are projected. Cut candidate if the pool is over target.

candidates.name: Dump-and-Bake Italian Sausage Rotini Casserole
candidates.why: Five ingredients, all board commodities, five minutes of prep and no boiling the pasta; verified 405 cal / 24g protein at 8 servings, so protein nearly clears and our portion takes calories over 500. DUPE RISK, flagging it for the selector: this shares sausage plus tomato plus pasta DNA with the live Italian Sausage Penne with Peppers, differing mainly by construction (oven, no peppers, rotini). If the selector is cutting to target, this is the fairest casualty in the slice. CONFIDENCE: est_cal projected.

candidates.name: Black-Eyed Pea Soup with Sausage and Kale
candidates.why: Verified 533 cal / 30g protein at the source, clears both bars as written, which is rare for a soup. Southern New Year's dish with no equivalent anywhere in the catalog. FLAGGED: black-eyed peas are the base and have no board id; canned-pinto-beans or canned-white-beans (both tracked) substitute mechanically but change the dish's identity, so this is worth a commodity registration rather than a swap. Everything else is board-tracked.
